source_text:
40 Πάντας μὲν εὐεργετεῖν
καλόν, μᾶλλον δὲ τοὺς μὴ δυναμένους ἀμείβεσθαι. 41Ῥήτωρ ἐν δικαιότητι ποτήριον
ψυχροῦ ὕδατος. 42 Σωφροσύνη καὶ πραΰτης ψυχῆς Χερουβίμ. 43 Τὸ εντιμον ἐν γήρᾳ
εἶναι ἀπόδειξις τοῦ φιλόπονον πρὸ γήρως γεγονέναι· τὸ σπουδαῖον ἐν νέῳ ἐχέγγυον
τοῦ εντιμον ἐν γήρᾳ εσεσθαι. 44Ὑπερῷον ψυχῆς θεωρία ἀληθής. 45 Φιλῶν ἃ μὴ δεῖ
οὐ φιλήσεις ἃ δεῖ. 46 Χρυσὸν κίβδηλον ἄμεινον ἢ φίλον κεκτῆσθαι. 47 Ψυχὴ καθαρὰ
μετὰ θεὸν θεός. 48Ὢ ἀπὸ τῆς φιλαυτίας τῆς πάντα μισούσης.
Aliae sententiae
49Ἀρχὴ ἀγάπης ὑπόληψις δόξης. 50 Καλὸν πλουτεῖν ἐν πραΰτητι καὶ ἀγάπῃ.
51 Λικμήτωρ ἀρετῆς λογισμὸς ὑπερήφανος. 52 Λεία ὁδὸς ὑπὸ ἐλεημοσύνης γίνεται.
53Ἄδικος δικαστὴς μεμολυσμένη συνείδησις. 54 ∆εινόν ἐστι πάθεσι δουλεύειν
σαρκός. 55 Εἰ θέλεις αλυπος ειναι, θεῷ ἀρέσκειν σπούδαζε. 56Ὁ καλῶς φροντίζων
ἑαυτοῦ φροντίζεται ὑπὸ θεοῦ. 57 Σώφρων καρδία λιμὴν θεωρημάτων.
thought_title: Virtue, friendship, and the soul's ascent
orientation: The speaker continues the alphabetical collection of spiritual maxims, now moving through sayings on benefaction, self-control, friendship, and the soul's relation to God.
pass_a_gloss: To benefit all men on the one hand is good, but rather those not able to repay. An orator in righteousness is a cup of cold water. Self-control and gentleness of soul are cherubim. The being honored in old age is a proof of the having been industrious before old age; the being earnest in a young man is a guarantee of the being honored in old age to be. An upper room of soul is true contemplation. Loving what one ought not, you will not love what one ought. Shining gold is better than a friend to possess. A pure soul after God is a god. O from the self-love that hates all things. Other sayings. Beginning of love is a thinking well of someone. Good it is to be rich in gentleness and love. A winnower of virtue is a proud thought. A smooth road by almsgiving comes to be. An unjust judge is a defiled conscience. Terrible it is to be enslaved to passions of flesh. If you wish to be without grief, to please God be eager. The one who cares well for himself is cared for by God. A self-controlled heart is a harbor of contemplations.

choices.term: Ῥήτωρ ἐν δικαιότητι ποτήριον ψυχροῦ ὕδατος
choices.english: An orator in righteousness is a cup of cold water
choices.why: Keeps the predicative structure and the abrupt, aphoristic equation of the Greek; 'orator' renders ῥήτωρ literally, and 'in righteousness' preserves the prepositional phrase.
rejected: A righteous speaker is a cup of cold water
An eloquent man in justice is a cup of cold water

choices.english: Self-control and gentleness of soul are cherubim
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'cherubim' and keeps the genitive ψυχῆς as 'of soul' to preserve the Greek's compactness.
rejected: Self-control and gentleness are the soul's cherubim
Self-control and gentleness of soul are angels

choices.term: Τὸ εντιμον ἐν γήρᾳ εἶναι ἀπόδειξις τοῦ φιλόπονον πρὸ γήρως γεγονέναι
choices.english: The being honored in old age is a proof of the having been industrious before old age
choices.why: Renders the articular infinitives literally as 'the being honored' and 'the having been industrious' to preserve the Greek's nominalized verbal force.
rejected: Being honored in old age proves one was industrious before old age
Honor in old age is proof of industry before old age

choices.english: An upper room of soul is true contemplation
choices.why: Keeps the word order and the predicative equation; 'upper room' renders ὑπερῷον literally, and 'contemplation' uses the glossary term.
rejected: True contemplation is the soul's upper room
The soul's upper room is true insight

choices.term: Χρυσὸν κίβδηλον ἄμεινον ἢ φίλον κεκτῆσθαι
choices.english: Counterfeit gold is better than a friend to possess
choices.why: Preserves the Greek's compressed comparison and the infinitive κεκτῆσθαι as 'to possess' at the end.
rejected: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a friend
Counterfeit gold is better to possess than a friend

choices.english: A pure soul after God is a god
choices.why: Keeps the stark predicative structure and the prepositional phrase 'after God' for μετὰ θεόν, preserving the theological paradox.
rejected: A pure soul is a god after God
A pure soul is second to God

pass_b_english: It is good to benefit everyone, but especially those who cannot repay. An orator in righteousness is a cup of cold water. Self-control and gentleness of soul are cherubim. To be honored in old age is proof of having been industrious before old age; earnestness in a young man is a guarantee that he will be honored in old age. The upper room of the soul is true contemplation. If you love what you ought not, you will not love what you ought. It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a counterfeit friend. A pure soul after God is a god. Alas for the self-love that hates all things!

The beginning of love is an opinion of glory. It is good to be rich in gentleness and love. A proud thought is the winnower of virtue. The road becomes smooth through almsgiving. An unjust judge is a defiled conscience. It is terrible to be enslaved to the passions of the flesh. If you wish to be without grief, strive to please God. The one who cares well for himself is cared for by God. A self-controlled heart is a harbor of contemplations.
notes: The source text contains several unaccented or inconsistently accented forms (e.g., εντιμον for ἔντιμον, εσεσθαι for ἔσεσθαι, αλυπος for ἄλυπος, ειναι for εἶναι, ανυδρος for ἄνυδρος in the following section), likely reflecting the manuscript's orthography; these are glossed according to their evident meaning.
The heading 'Aliae sententiae' appears in Latin in the source, marking a new subsection of sayings.

problems.ruling: μετὰ + accusative here means 'next to/after in rank' (LSJ μετά B.III.2), not temporal 'after'.

edits.old: A pure soul after God is a god.
edits.new: A pure soul with God is a god.

fixed: Changed 'after God' to 'with God' because μετὰ θεὸν means 'with God' (accompaniment), not 'after God'.

problems.why: κίβδηλον means shining or glittering, not counterfeit.
problems.fix: It is better to possess shining gold than a friend.

problems.why: δόξα here means 'opinion/reputation' not 'glory'; ὑπόληψις δόξης = 'esteem/reputation', i.e., thinking well of someone
problems.fix: The beginning of love is thinking well of someone
problems.ruling: δόξα = opinion/reputation; "glory" misstates meaning, altering nuance of phrase.

edits.old: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a friend.
edits.new: It is better to possess shining gold than a friend.

edits.old: The beginning of love is the supposition of glory.
edits.new: The beginning of love is thinking well of someone.

fixed: κίβδηλον means shining or glittering, not counterfeit; changed 'counterfeit gold' to 'shining gold'.
δόξα here means 'opinion/reputation' not 'glory'; ὑπόληψις δόξης = 'thinking well of someone'; changed 'the supposition of glory' to 'thinking well of someone'.

problems.why: κίβδηλον means counterfeit/fake, not shining; sense reversed
problems.fix: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a friend
problems.ruling: κίβδηλον means counterfeit/fake; translation 'shining gold' reverses meaning.

problems.quote: The beginning of love is thinking well of someone.
problems.why: Greek says ‘the beginning of love is an opinion of glory’, not ‘thinking well of someone’. The meaning is changed.
problems.fix: The beginning of love is an opinion of glory.
problems.ruling: Greek 'ὑπόληψις δόξης' = 'opinion of glory/reputation', not 'thinking well of someone'. Meaning lost.

edits.old: It is better to possess shining gold than a friend.
edits.new: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a friend.

edits.old: The beginning of love is thinking well of someone.
edits.new: The beginning of love is an opinion of glory.

fixed: κίβδηλον means counterfeit/fake, not shining; the English reversed the sense, so changed to counterfeit gold.
ὑπόληψις δόξης means an opinion/supposition of glory, not thinking well of someone; changed to an opinion of glory.

problems.quote: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a friend.
problems.source_quote: Χρυσὸν κίβδηλον ἄμεινον ἢ φίλον κεκτῆσθαι.
problems.why: In Greek, κίβδηλον ('counterfeit') applies to both gold and friend; omitting it before 'friend' absurdly says fake gold is better than any friend.
problems.fix: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a counterfeit friend.
problems.ruling: κίβδηλον pairs with φίλον in the comparison; English leaves friend unqualified, so fake gold beats any friend.

problems.quote: A pure soul with God is a god.
problems.why: μετά with the accusative (θεόν) means 'after' or 'next to' in rank, not 'with' (which requires the genitive).
problems.fix: A pure soul is, after God, a god.
problems.ruling: μετὰ θεὸν is accusative after/next in rank, not μετὰ genitive accompaniment rendered as with.

problems.quote: O, from the self-love that hates all things.
problems.source_quote: Ὢ ἀπὸ τῆς φιλαυτίας τῆς πάντα μισούσης.
problems.why: 'O, from...' is an unintelligible literal calque of the Greek exclamation of woe or aversion.
problems.fix: Alas for the self-love that hates all things!
problems.ruling: Ὢ is woe or repudiation, not O, from; the calque hides the force of φιλαυτία πάντα μισούσης.

edits.old: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a friend.
edits.new: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a counterfeit friend.

edits.old: A pure soul with God is a god.
edits.new: A pure soul after God is a god.

edits.old: O, from the self-love that hates all things.
edits.new: Alas for the self-love that hates all things!

fixed: counterfeit gold: added elided counterfeit before friend, since praising fake gold over any friend contradicts the work on friendship.
pure soul: changed with to after for μετὰ θεὸν with accusative meaning next in rank.
self-love exclamation: replaced unintelligible O, from with Alas for to render Ὢ ἀπὸ as woe/aversion.

refereed.quote: It is better to possess counterfeit gold than a friend
refereed.source_quote: Χρυσὸν κίβδηλον ἄμεινον ἢ φίλον κεκτῆσθαι
refereed.why: Missing 'counterfeit' on friend: better to have counterfeit gold than a counterfeit friend.
refereed.fix: Better to possess counterfeit gold than a counterfeit friend.
refereed.ruling: κίβδηλον means 'shining, glittering', not 'counterfeit'; translation changes meaning.
